Potassium Deficiency.shortDescription: Orange-yellow scorching along leaflet margins of older fronds giving a characteristic 'burnt leaf' appearance due to low soil potassium.
Potassium Deficiency.shortRemedy: Apply Muriate of Potash (MOP/KCl) per CRI schedule using split application. Add 500 g extra MOP if deficiency persists. Improve soil with compost and maintain balanced NPK.
causes: Heavy rainfall causing leaching in sandy or lateritic soils
Imbalanced fertilization — excess Ca or Mg reduces K uptake
symptoms: Rust or brown spotting on leaf edges
Leaf edges become dry and scorched

steps: Apply Muriate of Potash (MOP / KCl) as per CRI fertilizer schedule
Use split application method
Apply additional 500 g MOP per tree together with the recommended fertilizer mixture
Add Dolomite if Mg imbalance also exists
Add organic matter — compost, husk, or coconut waste
Maintain balanced NPK based on soil testing results

references: Coconut Research Institute of Sri Lanka (CRI) — Advisory Circulars – Fertilizer Recommendations. https://cri.gov.lk/en/advisory-circulars/
Good Hands Initiative — Nutrient Deficiencies in Coconut Trees. https://goodhands.lk/en/nutrient-deficiencies-in-coconut-trees-not-second-to-pests-and-diseases-2/

Magnesium Deficiency.shortDescription: Interveinal chlorosis of older fronds with yellow margins and a persistent green midrib giving a striped 'barber pole' appearance.
Magnesium Deficiency.shortRemedy: Apply 500 g Dolomite per tree with the recommended fertilizer mixture. For persistent cases add 500 g MOP. Long term: 1 kg Dolomite per bearing tree per year.
causes: Excess potassium fertilizer blocking Mg uptake
Nutrient leaching due to heavy rainfall
symptoms: Midrib stays green, creating a striped leaf appearance

steps: Apply Dolomite (500 g per coconut tree or seedling) together with the recommended fertilizer mixture
Apply additional 500 g Muriate of Potash (MOP) per tree along with fertilizer and Dolomite
Apply fertilizer around the fertilizer circle
For Mg deficiency trees: apply fertilizer on one half of circle, apply ~1 kg Kieserite on opposite half
Apply 1 kg Dolomite per bearing tree per year
Apply 500 g Dolomite per young coconut plant every 6 months

references: Coconut Research Institute of Sri Lanka (CRI). https://cri.gov.lk/
Good Hands Initiative — Nutrient Deficiencies in Coconut Trees. https://goodhands.lk/en/nutrient-deficiencies-in-coconut-trees-not-second-to-pests-and-diseases-2/

Yellow Patches.shortDescription: Small yellow spots on leaves that enlarge into brown lesions with dark margins and yellow halos, caused by fungal pathogens under humid conditions.
Yellow Patches.shortRemedy: Remove and destroy infected leaves immediately. Improve air circulation through spacing and pruning. Apply copper-based fungicide only in severe cases. Maintain balanced fertilization.
causes: Fungal pathogens: Septoria spp., Colletotrichum spp., Exserohilum spp.
High humidity and wet leaves for prolonged periods
Poor air circulation in overcrowded plantations
symptoms: Dark brown margins appear around spots
Spots merge into large dead patches
Leaf drying and premature leaf fall

steps: Remove infected leaves immediately and destroy them
Collect and destroy fallen infected debris
Improve air circulation through appropriate plant spacing and pruning
Avoid overhead irrigation that wets the foliage
Apply copper-based fungicide as a foliar spray
Repeat application as per product label if infection persists
Maintain balanced NPK and micronutrient fertilization to strengthen disease resistance

references: Coconut Research Institute of Sri Lanka (CRI) — Pests and Diseases Advisory Circulars. https://cri.gov.lk/en/advisory-circulars/
Good Hands Initiative — Coconut Leaf Blight Disease. https://goodhands.lk/en/coconut-leaf-blight-disease/
CORD — Coconut Research and Development Journal. https://journal.coconutcommunity.org/

Black Beetle Attack.shortDescription: Oryctes rhinoceros beetles bore into the growing crown and young fronds, causing characteristic V-shaped cuts, frass in the crown, and potential death of young palms.
Black Beetle Attack.shortRemedy: Remove all decaying logs and organic debris (breeding sites). Inspect palms regularly and extract beetles with a metal hook. Apply coal tar or naphthalene balls in leaf axils as repellents every 2 months.
causes: Oryctes rhinoceros beetles attack coconut crown
Beetle breeds in decaying organic matter: coconut logs, manure pits, compost heaps, coir dust piles, and dead palms
Adults bore into spear leaf and growing point
symptoms: V-shaped or wedge-shaped cuts on emerging leaves
Frass (fibrous waste material) visible in crown
Deformed and tattered fronds after expansion
Severe infestation can kill young palms

steps: Remove and destroy all decaying coconut logs and stumps
Clean and properly manage manure pits and compost heaps
Eliminate all potential breeding sites within and around the plantation
Inspect young palms regularly for signs of attack
Remove adult beetles from the crown using a metal hook
Apply coal tar or used engine oil in leaf axils — repeat every ~2 months
Place 6 naphthalene balls per palm in inner leaf axils

remedies.category: Chemical Control (Severe Cases Only — CRI Dosages)
steps: Seedlings: Carbofuran 3% at 15 g per plant, or Carbosulfan 10% at 10 g per plant
Young palms: Carbofuran 3% at 30 g per plant, or Carbosulfan 10% at 15 g per plant
Mix insecticide with equal quantity of sand and place in leaf axils — repeat monthly if necessary
Apply Metarhizium anisopliae fungus in beetle breeding sites
Install pheromone traps throughout the plantation to monitor and reduce adult beetle population

references: Coconut Research Institute of Sri Lanka (CRI) — Pest Management Advisory Circulars. https://cri.gov.lk/en/advisory-circulars/
University of Hawaiʻi — Coconut Rhinoceros Beetle Research. https://www.crbhawaii.org/
